These are allegations. Wang has pleaded not guilty and the verdict was postponed in June 2026 (Global News). Security incident coded Confirmed on the basis of the charges and Hydro-Quebec's own complaint; a reviewer may prefer Suspected until a verdict.
Timeline: CBC says the offences were allegedly committed between February 2018 and October 2022; Hydro-Quebec's corporate security complained to the RCMP in August 2022, so discovery is about 4 years after the begin date. He had worked there since October 2016 and was fired after the complaint. dbir_year 2019 follows the February 2018 begin date; this is an old incident surfaced by the 2025 trial coverage.
Discovery: internal (corporate security branch complaint); the detection method is not given, so Unknown.
Data: proprietary battery and energy-storage research, coded Secrets; no record count.
Victim: Hydro-Quebec, Quebec's provincially owned electric utility, NAICS 221111 (hydroelectric generation, from issue body 22111). Government Regional (provincial crown corporation). About 21,000 employees (company annual report figure, approximate) -> 10001 to 25000.
Asset hosting unknown.

event_chain.summary: Privilege abuse: proprietary research shared with Chinese institutions

summary: Yuesheng Wang, a battery researcher at Hydro-Quebec's transportation electrification and energy storage centre (CETEES), is accused of using his position between February 2018 and October 2022 to pass proprietary Hydro-Quebec research to Chinese universities and research centres, publishing scientific papers and filing patents with them instead of with his employer. Hydro-Quebec's corporate security branch complained to the RCMP in August 2022, Wang was fired and was charged in November 2022 with economic espionage, fraudulent use of a computer, fraudulently obtaining a trade secret and breach of trust. His trial began in October 2025; the verdict had been postponed as of June 2026. He has pleaded not guilty.
